skill.description: This Leadsets authoring template outlines usage checks, paginated searches, and email verification rules for prospecting skills. It leaves the search inputs, workflow steps, and output format for the author to define.
skill.summary: A starter template for writing a Leadsets prospecting skill.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The shell and reconnaissance alerts match Markdown and template text, not executable commands or system discovery. The documented Leadsets connection sends queries to an external service, and the draft leaves search scope and total record use undefined. No evidence of credential exfiltration or audit-targeted prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: The template relies on defaults that it does not define.
remediation.suggestion: Define required filters and a total record cap. Ask for approval before any external call if the account, search scope, or budget is unclear.

remediation.issue: The workflow depends on an external service for prospect data.
remediation.suggestion: Identify which request fields go to Leadsets. Keep credentials in the client configuration and send only the fields required for the authorized search.

semantic_findings.title: Search scope and record spend lack defined defaults
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells agents to use defaults instead of asking, but the input section does not define them. The quota check does not cap record use for an individual run. Completing the workflow by guessing could broaden the search and consume records the user did not authorize.

content.value_statement: Prospecting skills need clear search inputs, record limits, and rules for labeling email results. This template offers a starting structure and documents how to handle those service responses.
actual_capabilities: Provides sections for triggers, inputs, steps, checks, and output.
Documents a usage check and a one-record filter test before larger searches.
Describes cursor pagination for people and company searches.
Documents when to retry rate-limited requests and when to stop.
Defines how to distinguish verified, catch-all, unknown, and invalid email results.
limitations: This is an authoring template, not a finished prospecting workflow.
Search defaults, arguments, output columns, and per-run record caps are not defined.
Live searches require a Leadsets account and an MCP connection or REST credentials.
The template does not supply a lead list or verify emails on its own.

use_cases.title: Outline a lead search
use_cases.description: Define the target roles, company filters, and search boundaries before turning the outline into a runnable workflow.

use_cases.title: Define contact status labels
use_cases.description: Plan how to display verified, catch-all, unknown, and invalid addresses without treating them as interchangeable.

use_cases.title: Review record spending rules
use_cases.description: Use the service guidance to draft quota checks, a per-run record cap, and conditions for stopping after an error.

prompt_templates.title: Identify template gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: List the sections I need to complete before using this Leadsets template. Do not connect to Leadsets.

prompt_templates.title: Draft search inputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: define the intended audience for a search.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft inputs for a search by role, company size, and country. Mark which values I must supply and leave all external calls disabled.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the output
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a contact status report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose output columns for a contact report. Keep verified, catch-all, unknown, and invalid statuses separate. Use fictional examples only.

prompt_templates.title: Review workflow safeguards
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare the draft for implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft for approval gates, record caps, retry limits, and stopping conditions. Identify where contact data would leave the workspace. Do not use external tools.

output_examples.input: Which parts of the template need decisions before it can be used?
output: Define required search filters and a total record cap.
Specify which fields the report will include and when the search must stop.
No external service calls were made.

output_examples.input: Draft status labels for a contact report.
output: Verified: Leadsets explicitly confirmed the address.
Catch-all: the domain accepts mail without confirming the specific mailbox.
Unknown and invalid: report these as separate statuses.

best_practices: Define search filters and a total record cap before connecting to Leadsets.
Check the remaining quota and review one result before requesting more pages.
Mark an email as verified only when the verification or enrichment response confirms it.
anti_patterns: Treating placeholder instructions as a complete workflow.
Paging through results without an approved total record cap.
Marking addresses from search results or old CRM entries as verified.

faq.question: Can this template find prospects as shipped?
faq.answer: No. An author must define the inputs, tool arguments, checks, and output before it becomes a usable workflow.

faq.question: Do I need a Leadsets account to edit the template?
faq.answer: No. An account is required only to run live Leadsets requests.

faq.question: How does a live workflow connect to Leadsets?
faq.answer: The template lists a hosted MCP server or a Leadsets API key for REST access.

faq.question: Why test a search with one record first?
faq.answer: A single result can reveal mismatched filters before a larger search consumes more records.

faq.question: What counts as a verified email?
faq.answer: Only an address that Leadsets marks as verified in a verification or enrichment response.

faq.question: What happens when the account reaches a limit?
faq.answer: The guide allows one retry for certain short rate limits. It says to stop when the weekly or free record limit is reached.
